newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NW Shelf expansion proceeds - Woodside.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NW Shelf expansion proceeds - Woodside.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday the North-West Shelf partners had agreed to a A$6.0 billion expansion of the gas project.
The company said its expansion plans include a 700,000 tonne per year increase in capacity.
Woodside said the plan for a two train liquefied natural gas expansion was submitted to the project's eight Japanese power and gas utility customers at a meeting in Osaka this week.

"The expansion would add approximately seven million tonnes per annum to the existing sales capacity of approximately 7.5 million tonnes per annum. Subject to the requirements of the buyers, the expansion could be onstream in 2003."

"In addition to the two new onshore trains to be located adjacent to the existing facilities in the Pilbara region of Western Australia, the expansion will involve new offshore production facilities and LNG shipping," the company said.
"The total cost of the LNG expansion is expected to be approximately A$6 billion."
Woodside said the Osaka meeting followed indications from buyers in June of their interest in an expansion of the North West Shelf project.
"The LNG expansion project allows for growth in domestic gas sales and extension of existing contracts," Woodside said.

Woodside is an equal 16.66 percent shareholder in the project along with BHP Petroleum (North West Shelf) Pty Ltd, BP Developments Australia Ltd, Chevron Asiatic Ltd, Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, and Japan Australia LNG (MIMI) Pty Ltd.
Woodside shares rose in response to the announcement and were five cents higher at A$8.80 at 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT).
